text.stageNote: In process order. Log where the miss was created, not where the customer noticed it.
tips: A missing item is usually found by packing or by the customer, but created earlier. Trace it back before you log it.
One order with three missing items is one incomplete order; put the detail in the note.
With orders shipped you get the incomplete rate, the share of complete orders, DPMO and sigma level.
text.checkIntro: Walk from the pick face to the vehicle and tick what you actually see today. Every unticked line is a place where an item or a parcel can go missing.

Receiving.meaning: Goods were booked in that never arrived, or arrived in a different quantity. Every pick from that stock comes up short later.
moves: Count at receiving against the delivery, not against the purchase order.
Use blind counts: the receiver counts first, then sees the expected quantity.
Book differences the same day, so the system never promises stock that is not there.
Receiving.question: Who counts the goods, and do they know the expected number before they count?

Replenishment.meaning: The pick face runs empty or gets the wrong item while the system still shows stock. Pickers short-pick or take the neighbour.
moves: Trigger replenishment before the face is empty, not after.
Scan location and item at every put-away to the pick face.
Start each shift with the faces that had repeated shorts the day before.
Replenishment.question: How does a picker find out a location is empty, and what do they do then?

Picking.meaning: The wrong item or the wrong quantity goes into the tote. Look-alike items, multi-unit lines and time pressure drive most of it.
moves: Scan every item and confirm the quantity on multi-unit lines.
Separate look-alikes: sizes, colours and variants of one product never side by side.
Make reporting a short pick faster than working around it.
Picking.question: What happens when the picker cannot find the full quantity?

Packing.meaning: An item is left on the table, slips into the next order or goes into the wrong box.
moves: Scan each item against the order before the box is closed.
One order on the table at a time, and a clear table before the next one.
Check the weight on orders where the expected weight is known.
Packing.question: How does the packer know the order is complete before closing the box?

Sorting and loading.meaning: Parcels of one order are separated: one goes on the vehicle, another stays behind or goes to the wrong route.
moves: Count parcels per order at loading: two of three is not loaded.
Scan every parcel onto the vehicle and check the scan-out against the route.
Sweep the sort area at the end of each wave for parcels left behind.
Sorting and loading.question: What stops the last parcel of an order from staying on the floor?

Delivery.meaning: Parcels stay in the vehicle, go to the wrong address, or only part of a multi-parcel order is handed over.
moves: Scan every parcel at handover and count multi-parcel orders at the door.
Check that the vehicle is empty at the end of the route.
Follow up every "not received" within a day, while the driver still remembers the stop.
Delivery.question: How does the driver know every parcel for this stop has been handed over?

causes.Stock accuracy: Cycle-count the locations behind the misses the same day, and find where the stock record went wrong, not only what the count is now.
causes.Pick error: Watch picks at the location with the most misses. Most pick errors are designed in by layout, labels and look-alike items.
causes.Pack error: Make the order visible at the packing table and scan against it. Memory does not hold at peak.
causes.Scan skipped: Ask why the scan was skipped. A slow scanner, a missing label or a target that punishes scanning time are more common than carelessness.
causes.Sort or load error: Count and scan at the vehicle door. Orders with more than one parcel need their own check.
causes.System or data: Check the master data: pack sizes, units of measure, bundles and kits often promise quantities the shelf does not hold.
causes.Unknown: A large Unknown share means the log is not yet good enough. Record where it went wrong and why at the moment a miss is found.

checklist: Every pick is scanned: location and item.
Quantities on multi-unit lines are counted and confirmed, not assumed.
Look-alike items are not stored next to each other.
Short picks are reported at once, not left for packing to find.
Packing scans each item against the order before the box is closed.
Only one order is on the packing table at a time.
Multi-parcel orders are counted and kept together before loading.
Locations with shortages are cycle-counted the same day.
Every vehicle is checked empty at the end of the route.
Every incomplete order is logged with where it went wrong and why.
